statement: Paper B Lemma 5.1 extends past its printed length five, decidably. No word of length six is a minimal certificate (no_minimal_certificate_six), which is why the certificate density is still 7/8 at depth six. Exactly three words of length seven are: OOEOOEE, OOOEOEE, OOOOEEE (minimal_certificates_seven). The depth-seven certificate density is therefore 115/128 = 7/8 + 3/128 (certifiedWordCount_seven, seven_step_density, seven_step_gain). The manuscript states nothing about lengths six or seven. This is combinatorics only: each of the three new words would need its own mixed-mode exponential-sum estimate before 115/128 became a density for the Juggler map rather than a count of words.

Paper B Theorems 5.2-5.4, assembly half. Let certifiedWords d be the length-d parity words with a contracting prefix. (i) Their counts are 13, 28, 56, 115 at d = 4, 5, 6, 7, so the certificate densities are 13/16, 7/8, 7/8, 115/128; depth six adds nothing. (ii) At depth five the cylinders of E, OE, OOEE, OOOEE, OOEOE have sizes 16, 8, 2, 1, 1, are pairwise disjoint, and their union is exactly certifiedWords 5 (five_cylinders_cover, five_cylinders_card_sum) — so the printed 1/2+1/4+1/16+1/32+1/32 = 7/8 is the cylinder arithmetic and not a free-standing rational identity (printed_measures_are_counts). (iii) For every N the starts in {1,...,N} certified by depth five number classCount E N + classCount OE N + classCount OOEE N + classCount OOOEE N + classCount OOEOE N (certifiedCount_five_eq), via sum_classCount_cylinder and itinerary_take. (iv) 5/6 < 23/24 < 47/48 < 127/128 < 1 with N^e <= N^f for e <= f and N >= 1, which is the absorption the proofs assume. (v) five_step_error_assembly: five class counts within errors of their main terms add to 7N/8 within the sum of the errors. Every analytic count is a hypothesis: Theorem 3.1 and Corollaries 4.6, 4.10, 4.12 are not proved here or anywhere in the repository, so this bounds no exponential sum and is not a density theorem or a termination statement.
